 Order

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 29.11.2013 passed by Member Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Betul District-Betul in MACC No.84/2012 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to paras-7 of impugned award, submits that on account of injuries sustained in the accident, appellant's right leg has been shortened by 9 inch and it does not also bend.
Tribunal has assessed permanent disability only 25%, which is on lower side.
Further, monthly income assessed by the Tribunal is also on the lower side.
No amount has been awarded for loss of amenities.
Amount awarded under other heads is also on the lower side.

Hence,
on above grounds, it is urged that appropriate amount be enhanced.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company submits that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.

Hence, no enhancement is required.
4.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

5. So far as loss of future earning capacity is concerned, as per para-7 of impugned award,
appellant's right leg has been shortened by 9 inches on account of injuries sustained in the accident and it does not also bend from knee.
Appellant was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
Tribunal has treated appellant as unskilled labour.
6. In view of nature of appellant's job, in this Court's opinion, loss of earning capacity should have been assessed as 50%.

In the instant case, accident occurred on 01.03.2012 and on 01.03.2012,
minimum wages of unskilled labour were Rs.4,545/- per month.
(Annual income Rs.54,540/-).
As appellant was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
Hence, multiplier of 18 is to be applied.

On Sanjay vs Vinod Kumar on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123331613/
2 application of above multiplier, total loss of earning capacity comes to Rs.9,81,720/- (18 x 54,540/-).
Thus, 50% loss of earning capacity would be Rs. 4,90,860/-.
Hence, appellant is entitled to Rs.4,90,860/- for loss of future earning capacity.
7. So far loss of amenities is concerned.
Tribunal has not awarded any amount under above head.
Taking into consideration the nature of disability as well as age of appellant, an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- is just and proper for loss of amenities.

8. So far as other heads are concerned, Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,000/-for nourishing diet,
Rs.3,000/- for pain and suffering.
Therefore, it would be just and proper to award Rs.25,000/- for conveyance/Attendant Charges, nourishing diet etc.
9. In view of discussion in the foregoing paras, appellant is entitled to receive Rs.4,90,860/- (loss of earning capacity) + Rs.2,00,000/- (loss of amenities) and Rs.25,000/- (conveyance etc.)

Thus,
appellant is entitled to receive an enhanced amount of (Rs.715860 - Rs. 3,13,464/-) Rs.4,02,396/-.
10.
Appellant has valued present appeal Rs.1,00,000/-, therefore, appellant shall pay deficit Court fees for remaining enhanced amount within three months.
The appellant shall be entitled to receive enhanced amount, only after payment of deficit Court fees.
11. Appeal partly allowed to the extent as indicated above.
